entries.identity_notes: Scoped to the exact two-family KL procedure analyzed by Csiszar and Tusnady. The information-projection alias is qualified here by KL direction and the two-family objective. It is not all block coordinate descent, arbitrary Bregman projection, or the later GAM framework permitting inexact parameter/distribution steps. Iterative proportional fitting and Sinkhorn scaling have their own margin constraints; sharing a projection interpretation does not identify the complete algorithms. claims.statement: Start with Q_0 in the second family. At each iteration choose P_n minimizing D(P||Q_(n-1)) over the first family, then Q_n minimizing D(P_n||Q) over the second. For probability laws, D(P||Q)=integral log(dP/dQ)dP, with infinity when absolute continuity fails. The two coordinate projections have different directions. Each displayed argmin must exist and be finite along the realized sequence; this is not supplied by the algorithm name. Exact steps cannot increase the paired objective.

evidence.locator: Section1 Eq1.1, pp205-208 / PDF1-4; Section3 Eq3.1 and Lemmas2-3, pp214-218 / PDF10-14

claims.statement: The convex-family KL construction has the three-point and four-point inequalities used to prove a five-point descent inequality. The objective tends to the infimum over the initialization-accessible first-family laws: those with finite D(P||Q_n) for some iterate. Equality of that infimum with the unrestricted one is an additional support/accessibility condition. Objective convergence is distinct from convergence of the distributions. In finite probability spaces, closed families are compact; analogous arguments for unnormalized measures need their own boundedness or compactness justification.

evidence.locator: Sections1-2, Theorems1-2, pp207-213 / PDF3-9; Section3 Theorem3 and subsequent proof, pp217-218 / PDF13-14

claims.statement: The paper also uses uncorrected D(P||Q) for finite measures, which can be negative when their masses differ. Its nonnegative auxiliary is D(P||Pprime)+Pprime(X)-P(X). That extension must not be silently treated as probability KL. The stopping-bound step that integrates log(dQ_n/dQ_(n-1)) against a minimizing P requires its total-mass factor unless P is normalized. A convergent Q sequence alone also does not force successive density ratios to approach one at coordinates whose limit is zero. The saved finite examples exhibit both issues.

evidence.locator: Section3 Eq3.1-3.3 and Eq3.11 discussion, pp214-219 / PDF10-15; curator finite-measure scaling and vanishing-coordinate examples

claims.statement: For incomplete-data fitting, a family of complete laws with prescribed observed marginal can be paired with a model-distribution family. Projection onto the prescribed marginal rescales the current joint law by the observed-to-current marginal ratio; the other projection fits the model to the completed law. A convex model-distribution family can inherit the global accessible-infimum result. Jointly parameterized nonconvex mixture or neural families do not become convex merely because they use EM.

evidence.locator: Section4 Theorem4 and Eq4.1-4.6, pp220-221 / PDF16-17; Section5A, pp226-230 / PDF22-26

claims.statement: For fixed component probabilities mu_i(y) and a target probability p(y), let q_c(y)=sum_i c_i mu_i(y). claims.statement: Under Theorem5: a probability target, finitely many fixed component measures, strictly positive simplex initialization and a finite best divergence, the coefficient vector converges to a vector attaining the minimum divergence. For fixed probability components in a finite observation space this is the convex mixture-weight likelihood problem. The proof does not require identifiable component representation, so the limit can depend on initialization; identical components preserve their initial relative weights. claims.statement: For finite source/reproduction alphabets, fixed source p(x), finite nonnegative distortion rho(x,y), multiplier beta>=0 and positive initial reproduction marginal q(y), set W(y|x)=q(y)exp(-beta*rho(x,y))/sum_z q(z)exp(-beta*rho(x,z)). Unused zero-probability source rows can be omitted.

claims.statement: Given a real-valued objective D and an initial Q_0 in family Q_0, at iteration n choose P_n in argmin over family P_n of D(P,Q_(n-1)), then Q_n in argmin over family Q_n of D(P_n,Q). claims.statement: Theorem4 assumes compact families within a common compact metric space, Hausdorff convergence to compact limiting families, continuous D, and its compatible three-point/four-point inequalities C1-C2. It first guarantees that the objective liminf equals the limiting global minimum and that cluster points of subsequences attaining that liminf are optimal. Full objective convergence and optimality of all cluster points additionally follow if sum_n omega_D(2epsilon_n) is finite, where epsilon_n is the sum of the two Hausdorff errors and omega_D is the modulus of continuity on the sum product metric. This is a sufficient condition, not a necessary one, and does not require a unique optimum or imply convergence of the entire point sequence.

The paper also modifies small empirical frequencies to maintain positivity, a correction that is eventually inactive under its iid assumptions. For the ordinary empirical convergence rate, the authors conclude liminf optimality and explicitly withhold the stronger full-convergence conclusion from this theorem.

csiszar.abstract_interpretation: Studies exact alternating minimization between convex families of finite measures, with KL and a five-point descent inequality. Objective convergence is to an initialization-accessible infimum; additional hypotheses give measure/weight convergence. Applications include incomplete-data likelihood, fixed-component mixture weights, channel capacity, rate distortion and expected-log portfolio fitting. This is not a general global-optimization result for nonconvex neural/model parameter families.
notes: PDF1-4 / pp205-208: alternating exact attained finite minima Pn->Qn->Pn+1 for a two-argument extended-real objective. Five-point property d(P,Q)+d(P,Q0)>=d(P,Q1)+d(P1,Q1) when Q0->P1->Q1. The accessible family P0 consists of P with d(P,Qn)<infinity for some n; reaching the unrestricted global infimum additionally requires its infimum equal that over all P. An arbitrary starting support is not harmless. Hilbert squared-distance and finite-measure KL applications are contextual examples.

PDF5-9 / pp209-213: Lemma1 telescoping bound with limsup bn>-infinity, at least one finite bn, and optional summability of negative deviations. Theorems1-2 give objective convergence under five-point property; three-point delta(P,P1)+d(P1,Q0)<=d(P,Q0) and four-point d(P,Q1)<=delta(P,P1)+d(P,Q) imply it. Delta nonnegative and zero on diagonal. For a global minimizing P, delta(P,Pn) is nonincreasing. Existence of the exact minimizing sequence is explicitly not proved in general. Objective convergence and convergence of both iterates are separate.

PDF9-10 / pp213-214: closed convex Hilbert sets with squared norm have the projection inequalities. Whole-sequence convergence proof additionally uses one compact set and projection continuity; arbitrary closed infinite-dimensional sets are not declared compact.

PDF10-14 / pp214-218: D(P||Q)=integral log(dP/dQ)dP, infinity without absolute continuity, for finite nonzero measures. This uncorrected finite-measure D can be negative; delta(P,Pprime)=D(P||Pprime)+Pprime(X)-P(X) is nonnegative. Lemmas2-3 prove three/four-point inequalities by convex mixtures and monotone-convergence differentiation. Theorem3 yields objective convergence on the accessible family; finite-X closed-set paragraph claims Pnconvergence and Qnconvergence on positive support of Pstar. Its proof assumes convergent subsequences from closed families; for arbitrary finite measures closed need not mean bounded. A Q sequence can vary without bound in coordinates invisible to P. This is a proof-scope concern, not yet a refutation of the Pn theorem; use finite probability/compact sets for any verified curation.

PDF15 / p219: stopping Eq3.11 upper-bounds objective gap by log sup_x(dQn/dQn-1), after bounding an integral against minimizing P. For a nonunit P this step needs P(X)factor; the printed formula is immediately justified for probability P. The further statement that convergent Qn makes the ratio supremum tend1 needs care at zero limiting coordinates. Construct bounded finite examples before asserting discrepancies. Adding integral c dP corresponds to exponential reweighting Q by exp(-c); normalized per-cost objective is a separate convention.

PDF16-18 / pp220-222: measurable-image lifting. A prescribed observed marginal defines the desired convex family; exact projection onto it rescales by marginal Radon-Nikodym ratio. Opposite direction also treated. Theorem4 retains accessible-infimum condition. Lemma4lifts k fixed measures onto a component-label product space: minimizing D(S||R_c) uses component masses S(i)/S(X); reverse direction uses exponential coefficients with measure masses and a normalization multiplier. Directions differ and zero-mass/support conventions matter.

PDF19-22 / pp223-226: Theorem5 fixed finite-component measure mixture Qc=sum_i ci*mui, positive simplex initialization and finite best divergence from a probability target. Update ci_new=ci_old*integral(dmui/dQold)dPtarget. Each update normalizes because target mass1. The proof gives convergence of coefficient vectors without requiring unique mixture representation, via KL Fejer monotonicity to a subsequential optimum. Limit may depend on initialization when representations are not unique. Gap bound max_i log(ci_new/ci_old) has active-support/zero-coefficient conventions; no arbitrary zero initialization is justified. Original component laws are fixed, not jointly fit unknown means/variances.

PDF22-26 / pp226-230: incomplete-data ML with fixed density versions and explicit dominating measures. Finite observed space gives empirical-distribution KL plus constant. Convex model-distribution family yields global objective result with accessible support conditions; nonconvex EM retains ascent but not global convergence. PDF24 / p228 says D is maximized by the same Q maximizing expected log likelihood, but displayed D=constant-L requires minimized; do not adopt that word. Continuous observations are handled by disintegrating a dominating measure and constructing a new finite measure over observed fibers, not naive KL between empirical Diracs and a continuous probability density. niesen.abstract_interpretation: Extends paired exact alternating minimization to domains that change with iteration, seeking the optimum of limiting domains rather than solving every transient problem fully. Presents sufficient compactness, continuity, projection-inequality and set-convergence conditions, with applications to mixture decomposition and signal processing. The formal theorem distinguishes a liminf result from stronger objective convergence requiring a summable continuity-error bound.
notes: PDF1-2/pp1423-1424: exact coordinate minimizations. At iteration n, Pn minimizes D(P,Qn-1) over current family P_n, then Qn minimizes D(Pn,Q) over current family Q_n. One coordinate sweep per revealed pair, not a fully converged inner solve for each n. Fixed families recover classical alternating minimization. D is a continuous real-valued objective on a compact metric product space; Hausdorff distance measures family convergence.

PDF3/p1425: C1 uses P and its first-coordinate minimizer in P_n with Q in Q_(n-1). C2 uses P and Ptilde in P_n, Q and its second-coordinate minimizer in Q_n. The same function delta must satisfy both; footnote3 explicitly does not require delta nonnegative. Theorem4 requires compact families contained in one compact ambient metric space, Hausdorff convergence to compact limiting families and continuous D. It gives objective liminf equal to the limiting global minimum; only subsequences achieving that liminf are initially certified optimal.

PDF3-5/pp1425-1427: Full objective convergence and optimality of all cluster points follow if sum_n omega_D(2epsilon_n)<infinity, epsilon_n=d_H(P_n,P)+d_H(Q_n,Q), omega on the sum product metric. This is sufficient, not proved necessary, and does not force a unique pair or convergence of the entire iterate sequence. Moving domains need not make the objective monotone. Proof telescopes approximate five-point inequalities and bounds by uniform continuity; Eq12 prose references Eq13 before its display, a harmless cross-reference issue not a scientific defect.
